hints: Velocity is the slope of the x–t curve. What is the slope at t = 0, and where is it zero?
worded:
1. Velocity is the slope of the x–t graph, so read slopes, not heights.

2. At t = 0 the curve heads downward at its steepest: the velocity starts at its most negative value.

3. At the lowest point of x the slope is zero, and after it the curve rises, so v becomes positive. At the top of x, v is zero again and then turns negative.

4. So v starts at a negative maximum, rises through zero, peaks, and comes back: a negative cosine shape. (C)

5. (B) and (D) start at v = 0, which would need a flat x–t curve at t = 0; (A) starts positive. All three are out.
conventional:
![](asset:P000165-sol-1)

The curve is $x = - A\sin\omega t$, so

$$v = \frac{dx}{dt} = - A\omega\cos\omega t,$$

which is $- A\omega$ at $t = 0$, zero when $x$ is lowest ($\omega t = \pi/2$), and so on: graph (C).
mistakes: Don’t copy the shape of the x–t graph: v is its slope, shifted by a quarter cycle.
